newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee tightly mixed, switches active.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee tightly mixed, switches active.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures were tightly mixed by midsession on Monday with activity centred on eleventh-hour rollover of July positions into September ahead of July's first tender day on Tuesday.
Traders also noted light roaster buying of distant November and January contracts.
"There have been some last minute July/Sept switch trades before the first notice day," said one. The spread traded at $22-$28 all morning against Friday's close at $15.
July's uncovered positions stood at 3,287 lots by the close of business on Friday, down 613 from a day earlier.
By the midday pause, July stood $5 down at $1,755 per tonne while September eased $3 at $1,780.
Other traded months were unchanged to $5 up.
Traders called New York arabica futures to open one to two cents higher.

Traders said Friday's U.S. Department of Agriculture's world coffee supply/demand estimates contained in its latest semi-annual Tropical Products: World Markets and Trade report were described as neutral.
But they noted a sharp downward revision in Indonesia's 1997/98 coffee crop to 4.6 million bags from 6.1 million previously.
Chartwise, analysts said LIFFE coffee should hold this month's range for the time being, but bearish chart indicators may soon start to pressure benchmark September lower.
"Momentum indicators remain oversold while the longer-term moving averages are generally heading lower and are above the market," said Adrian Haylor, an analyst at Sucden.
"But the market is fairly well balanced and in the short term the range will probably continue to hold."
But a close below $1,700 would be crucial and signal a possible slide down to $1,550, he said.
